verdict_headline: NOT a sign-in attempt on a disabled identity. The writes are the UI walker's own tool arming its row to active, signing in successfully during the walk -- which is what writes updatedAt -- and disarming it again. Zero sign-ins were refused for a disabled account in any of the three windows, against working controls.
verdict_evidence_in_order: 1. THE IDENTITY IS THAT ACCOUNT. .claude/skills/ui-walk/SKILL.md:29 names the row by key and address and states it sits at status disabled at rest with a password hash nobody knows, role admin, internal, userType Dev -- which matches the row's own firmId, role and userType as read.

2. THE TOOL'S OWN WRITES DO NOT TOUCH updatedAt. ui_walker_account.py has exactly three update paths: arm's lease (line 136, SET armedBy, armedAt), arm's activation (line 151, SET passwordHash and status), and disarm (line 185, SET passwordHash and status, REMOVE armedBy and armedAt). NONE sets updatedAt. So the moving updatedAt is not written by the arm or the disarm themselves.
3. BUT THE ARM MAKES THE ROW ACTIVE. arm sets status active for the length of one walk, mints a random password into SSM, and prints a holder id.

4. A SUCCESSFUL SIGN-IN IS THE ONLY WRITER OF updatedAt IN THE SIGN-IN SOURCE. db.ts:271-284 updateLastLogin issues UpdateExpression 'SET lastLogin = :now, updatedAt = :now' against PK/SK PROFILE, and it is the only place either field is written. Its single call site is auth.ts:204, inside mintSession.

5. AND IT IS UNREACHABLE BY A DISABLED ROW. mintSession is called only after the status guard at auth.ts:106 (the other guards are 255 and 538). A row that is not status active is refused before a session is minted, so a REFUSED attempt cannot write updatedAt by this path.

6. THE ROW'S OWN TWO TIMESTAMPS ARE EQUAL. lastLogin == updatedAt exactly. Since one statement sets both to a single :now, the most recent write to this row WAS that statement -- a minted session -- and the row must therefore have been ACTIVE at that moment, i.e. inside an armed window.

7. NO SIGN-IN WAS REFUSED FOR BEING DISABLED. In each of the three ten-minute windows the quoted pattern for the disabled refusal returns 0, against unfiltered controls of 108, 72 and 40 events. A zero with a matching control is an absence.

8. THE WRONG-PASSWORD REFUSALS ARE THE TOOL'S OWN. Each window carries exactly one 'Invalid email or password', which is what disarm does by design: after replacing the hash it attempts a login with the dead walk password and requires a refusal (ui_walker_account.py:202-206, escalating if it is NOT refused).
9. THE ROW IS NOW AT REST. The one permitted status read prints status=disabled, armed=no, armedBy=none, so an arm/disarm cycle completed and the lease was returned.

10. NOTHING SCHEDULES IT. 156 EventBridge rules as a printed denominator with no unread page and the filter applied client-side: 0 name a walk. No crontab on this box. 0 hits across 513 .tools files. A TOOL runs as this identity, invoked by a seat; no schedule does.
what_would_move_this_verdict: The one thing the row cannot show is WHICH client authenticated during an armed window: a successful session was minted while the row was active, and by construction the walk password lives only in SSM and is read in-process by the walker (SKILL.md:31), but the row carries no actor field. A sign-in log line naming the authenticating client, or the SSM parameter's own access record, would close that; neither was read here. If such a read showed a client other than a walk, the verdict would move to ANOTHER_WRITER.

history_the_table_holds.stream_detail: describe-table reports StreamSpecification null and LatestStreamArn null on opal-users-v2, so there is NO change stream and no per-write record of what each write set.
history_the_table_holds.pitr_detail: describe-continuous-backups reports PointInTimeRecoveryStatus ENABLED. I had written DISABLED from assumption before reading it; the read says otherwise and this is the corrected value.
history_the_table_holds.does_either_answer_who_wrote_it: NOT AS READ, and the two settings answer different questions. The absence of a stream means there is no record of individual writes. PITR being ENABLED means the table's prior STATES are recoverable in principle -- a restore to just before each write would show WHICH ATTRIBUTES changed, which my projections cannot. But PITR records state, not actors: DynamoDB's point-in-time recovery would not name the caller even if restored. So the ACTOR is not obtainable from the table by any means available here, and WHAT CHANGED is obtainable only by a restore. NOTHING WAS ENABLED AND NOTHING WAS RESTORED: the order forbids both, a restore creates a new table and is far outside a read, and I did not do it. It is named as an available but unused instrument so the next seat knows the option exists and what it would and would not show.

No token, secret, credential, password hash, reset token or one-time code was read, printed or copied. passwordHash is named as an attribute and its value never touched.
No stream, export or recovery setting was changed. Both history settings were read and left off.
WHICH client authenticated inside an armed window is NOT established -- see what_would_move_this_verdict. The sign-in log lines were COUNTED, never printed, so no actor was extracted from them.
Whether writes earlier than 2026-10-11T22:41:40Z exist is not known: with no stream and no point-in-time recovery, only the writes my own reads straddled are visible, and there may be more.
The row of digest 1af514167abb (row D2-S53) was not read, named or probed by this order.

One inconsistency inside the ui-walk skill was noticed and NOT pursued, as it is that skill's and not this order's: SKILL.md:30 says disarm never deletes the SSM parameter, while ui_walker_account.py's own usage line says SSM is deleted. The status read prints SSM PRESENT. Reported here as an observation, with no row filed against TCKT_VNEXT.
